docs.title: Phi-Genesis — Limiting Spectral Constant
docs.text:
Phi-Genesis studies spectral operators on recursively refined Sierpiński-gasket graphs. Its principal result is a Lean 4 proof that the least-eigenvalue sequence selected by an exact Schur boundary recursion converges to a limit in an exact rational interval of width \(2\cdot10^{-36}\).

The detailed theorem and its boundaries are documented in the Schur recursion and limiting spectral constant dossier.

Open the interactive Phi-Genesis spectral-limit portal

For formal dependencies, see the Lean proof map. For numerical computations, see the high-precision note.

docs.title: Phi-Genesis Research Programmes
docs.text: The principal mathematical result is the convergence theorem for the least eigenvalues of the recursively defined Sierpiński-gasket graph operators.

docs.title: Schur recursion and limiting spectral constant
docs.text:
An exact three-corner boundary Schur recursion is connected to the graph matrices in Lean 4. Its selected root is the least eigenvalue for every level \(N\geq6\), and the sequence converges to \(\lambda_\infty\) inside an exact rational interval of width \(2\cdot10^{-36}\).

See the spectral-limit dossier, Lean proof map, and formal source files.

docs.title: Supporting mathematical and computational strands
docs.text:
• Signed local-face operator and gauge equivalence.
  • Spectral decimation and finite-level gap structure.
  • Boundary conditions and flux calculations.
  • Spectral dimension and finite-level counting.
  • Exact finite signed-\(Z_2\) H10 moment calculations.

Each strand retains its own proof or computation boundary and does not replace the main Schur-limit theorem.

docs.title: Verification layers
docs.text:
The project combines unit tests, numerical cross-checks and preregistered statistical tests. These answer different questions:

  • A unit test checks a specific implementation property.
  • A dense-spectrum comparison checks a numerical path against a smaller reference instance.
  • A preregistered null test evaluates whether a search result exceeds the specified chance baseline.
  • A theoretical derivation is needed for a general mathematical statement.

Passing one layer does not automatically establish claims that belong to another.

docs.title: D₃ representation audit for Open Problem #1
docs.text: Status: exploratory numerical diagnostic, reproduced on 7 November 2026. This is not a preregistered selection rule, a Lean theorem, or a proof that no spectral selection rule can exist.

docs.title: Scope and indexing
docs.text:
The calculation uses the same level-m Sierpiński-gasket graph and the unweighted corner-degree-2 combinatorial Laplacian constructed by phi_genesis.sg_laplacian.sierpinski_graph. The four target labels {1, 12, 17, 40} are 1-based positions in the positive spectrum, as specified in PREREGISTRATION.md: the constant zero eigenvalue is removed first.

This convention matters. In the earlier exploratory D₃ script, the full spectrum was clustered from its first entry (the zero eigenvalue) while targets were read as w[t - 1]. That assigned the zero mode to target 1 and shifted every positive target by one. The table below corrects that off-by-one error.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
At level m, represent a vertex by integer barycentric coordinates (p,q,r) with p+q+r=2^m. Permuting these three coordinates gives the six elements of D₃ ≅ S₃. The implementation verifies that each induced permutation is bijective and preserves the complete edge set.

For each numerically clustered eigenspace V_lambda, the code computes the six character traces of the restricted permutation action. The multiplicities of the irreducible representations are recovered from the character inner products:

  • A1: the trivial one-dimensional representation;
  • A2: the sign one-dimensional representation;
  • E: the two-dimensional standard representation.

The low eigenspaces are computed with SciPy's dense symmetric subset eigensolver. This is intentional: an iterative sparse solver can return an incomplete basis from a highly degenerate eigenspace, which would make its character trace incorrect. Eigenvalue clusters are grouped numerically with absolute tolerance 1e-8; the resulting classifications are computational, not exact-arithmetic certificates.

Reproduce from the repository root:

python -m phi_genesis.symmetry_probe
pytest -q test_symmetry_probe.py

docs.title: Corrected results
docs.text:
The complete cluster signature (cluster endpoints and A1, A2, E multiplicities) for the first 60 positive-spectrum positions is identical at levels 5, 6, and 7. The six D3 actions were verified as graph automorphisms at each of those levels.

Target rank Positive-spectrum cluster Multiplicity Representation lambda, level 5 lambda, level 6 lambda, level 7 1 1–2 2 E 0.005741958474563 0.001154094053506 0.000231192288259 12 12–14 3 A1 + E 0.143567179457051 0.028880249655440 0.005782737942710 17 16–17 2 E 0.200112150540496 0.040496798530680 0.008122335554676 40 30–41 12 3A1 + A2 + 4E 0.697224362268003 0.143567179457049 0.028880249655436

Here the last three columns give the eigenvalue of the full cluster containing the indicated target rank; all ranks in one cluster have that same eigenvalue within the stated numerical clustering tolerance.

The simple, fully symmetric (A1) eigenspaces in the first 60 positive-spectrum positions begin at

3, 9, 18, 27, 48, 54.

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text:
Two different symmetry criteria should not be conflated:

  1. Contains an A1 component: this criterion hits target ranks 12 and 40, because their complete eigenspaces contain A1. It does not hit 1 or 17. It selects whole degenerate eigenspaces (12–14 and 30–41), not the individual integer ranks.
  2. Is a simple, fully symmetric eigenspace: none of the four target ranks meets this criterion. The list of simple A1 ranks above does not contain any of the four targets.

Thus the earlier claim that positive-spectrum ranks 12 and 17 are both pure E, while rank 1 is fully symmetric, was incorrect. The corrected result does not select {1,12,17,40}. It is a bounded negative result for these two natural D3 criteria only. It does not rule out every possible function of the spectrum, every operator family, or a future independently derived physical selection mechanism.

docs.title: Protocol v1.3 archive: pending source verification
docs.text:
A previous conversation summary reports a separate ancestry/decimation selection probe and gives selected-count and target-mask claims for levels 6 and 7. However, the ZIP archive and its source files/results are not present in the inspected repository or among the files available for this audit. Consequently those claims have not been independently rerun here, are not part of the verified table above, and are not added to the cumulative count of documented configuration evaluations.

To verify v1.3, the archive (or its complete source code, frozen inputs, and expected outputs) must be added to the repository. The check should reproduce the archived outputs from the specified graph, operator convention, positive-spectrum indexing, and tolerances before the result is promoted from pending to verified.

docs.title: Reopening condition
docs.text:
Reopen the finite selection search only when at least one of the following is supplied:

  • the complete v1.3 archive and a reproducible independent check;
  • a new operator family with an a-priori mathematical rationale, a frozen selection statistic, a null-only power analysis, and a preregistration made before target evaluation;
  • a derivation of the target indices from an operator invariant that is independent of the masses used to identify the targets.

The four-mass fit remains a numerical fit, not a spectral prediction, until an independent rule is derived.

docs.title: Data, Provenance and Research Records
docs.text: Phi-Genesis maintains a distinction between source code, committed numerical artifacts, protocol commitments and later interpretation. This separation is essential because the research includes negative findings and reassessments of earlier apparent matches.

docs.title: Authoritative record hierarchy
docs.text:
1. Preregistration — the question, target set, rule, null ensembles, parameters and decision threshold fixed before evaluation.
  2. Code and data — the implementation, seeds, null pools and numerical outputs used in the test.
  3. Protocol ledger — the cumulative account of tested configurations, including exploratory and abandoned branches.
  4. Methodology — explanation of the statistical reasoning and interpretation limits.
  5. README and changelog — project-level summary and version history.
  6. Website and interactive portal — navigational and explanatory views, subordinate to the primary records.

docs.title: Current documented record
docs.text:
The current public project status is v2.2.1. The cumulative protocol ledger records 193 main-family configuration evaluations and an earlier carpet search of about 128 level-3 configurations plus an unrecorded level-4 sweep. Therefore the honest cumulative count is at least about 321, not a falsely precise total.

The carpet branch is marked abandoned after a null analysis reassessed its initial 4/4 match as consistent with a look-elsewhere effect. Protocol v1.0's power limitation is also explicitly documented; it is not treated as an informative negative.

docs.title: Provenance and limitations
docs.text:
• Do not present the four target indices as independently derived from the spectral operator.
  • Do not treat all target hits as equally informative: the base-rate audit found index 1 to be common under the tested ratio rule.
  • Do not describe the η-invariant value −4 as reproduced; the documented tests did not observe it.
  • Do not transfer the Lean verification status of Evgeny's Theorem to the separate Phi-Genesis computations.
  • Report finite graph level, operator convention, boundary conditions, estimator and numerical range with quantitative claims.

docs.title: Research Dissertation
docs.text:
Recursive Graph Operators, Spectral Trace Defects, and Higher-Moment Recurrence

Bibliographic field Record Author Evgeny Zaprudnov Research group RFT-SIRM Correspondence evgeniyzaprudnov@gmail.com Version 1.0 Date shown in the source 15 October 2026 Canonical manuscript DISSERTATION.md Source repository Evgeny's Theory of Everything

!!! info "Why the complete manuscript stays in its original repository" The dissertation contains mathematical notation, formulas, proof boundaries, finite-level certificates, numerical tables, and references. Linking to the canonical source avoids maintaining a second, potentially divergent copy inside Phi-Genesis. This page provides context and direct navigation; it is not a replacement manuscript.

docs.title: What the dissertation covers
docs.text: Strand Subject Evidence boundary Recursive graph operators Graph approximations and operator constructions on the Sierpiński gasket Definitions and results are scoped to the stated construction Fourth-moment trace defect A concrete identity for a specified SU(2)-connected operator The source project reports a Lean 4 formalization for the concrete proposition Higher even moments \(H^6\), \(H^8\), and \(H^{10}\) coefficient/recurrence research Finite-level certificates and numerical holdouts are not the same as an all-level proof Signed-flux spectral work \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-flux, spectral decimation, and boundary/corner corrections This is a distinct operator programme; Gate A and the mass-index rule remain open in Phi-Genesis Research methodology Reproducibility, explicit exceptions, numerical holdouts, and open problems Claims must be interpreted at the evidence level recorded in the source

docs.title: A mathematical anchor: the fourth-moment identity
docs.text:
The theorem repository states the following identity for its specified operators and assumptions:

\[ \Delta_m(H^4,\theta) =\operatorname{Tr}(H_C^4)-\operatorname{Tr}(H_{C'}^4) =-16\left(3^{m-1}+1\right)\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad m\ge1. \]

The normalized quantity is defined as

\[ I_m(\theta)=\frac{\Delta_m(H^4,\theta)}{3^{m+1}+3}, \qquad \lim_{m\to\infty}I_m(\theta) =-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

At \(\theta=\pi/2\), the limiting value is \(-8/9\).

!!! warning "Scope of the theorem" The formula above belongs to the concrete fourth-moment proposition in the Evgeny-Theorem source repository. It does not, by itself, establish the higher-moment all-level recurrence, close Phi-Genesis Gate A, derive the indices \(\{1,12,17,40\}\), prove a physical mass law, or establish a complete physical Theory of Everything.

docs.title: How this relates to Phi-Genesis
docs.text:
The two projects are related research strands, but they use different mathematical objects and answer different questions.

Evgeny-Theorem / dissertation strand Phi-Genesis strand Operator focus A specified SU(2)-connected graph operator Signed \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-flux / \(\pi\)-flux Laplacians Main observable Fourth-moment trace defect and related higher-moment questions Low-lying spectrum, gaps, decimation, and candidate mass indices Strongest stated evidence A concrete fourth-moment Lean formalization; finite-level higher-moment certificates and holdouts Reproducible numerical checks and preregistered selection searches Key unresolved question Proving the proposed higher-moment recurrence for all stated levels/angles from the recursive structure Characterizing the full decimation exceptional set and deriving target indices independently Does one establish the other? No No

A formal proof in one repository does not transfer automatically to another operator, observable, or physical interpretation. A bridge between these constructions would need its own definitions, assumptions, derivation, and verification.

docs.text: This page records the role of finite-level experiments in the Phi-Genesis research programme. They are computational checks on specified graph families and parameter choices, not physical-device experiments.

docs.title: Independent Verification and Test Boundaries
docs.text: Phi-Genesis is a spectral-computation project and does not claim to perform seL4 kernel verification. This page documents the analogous evidence boundary: computational tests validate only the specified implementation, operator, configuration, and parameter range.

docs.title: What a test can support
docs.text:
• Reproduction of a finite numerical observation.
  • Detection of implementation errors covered by the test.
  • A documented negative result for the tested family and decision rule.

docs.title: What it cannot support by itself
docs.text:
• An all-level mathematical theorem.
  • A physical mass-generation mechanism.
  • An independent selection rule for \(\{1,12,17,40\}\).
  • A claim about software or hardware systems not tested by the project.

For the actual computational methods and results, see Verified Results and Computational Architecture.

docs.title: Spectral anchor
docs.text:
For the Sierpiński gasket, the theoretical spectral exponent is

\[ \frac{d_s}{2}=\frac{\ln 3}{\ln 5}\approx 0.6826. \]

The factor-five scaling is a reference structure for finite-level spectral-decimation experiments. The corner-degree-2 graph Laplacian requires the documented corner-defect corrections.

docs.title: Boundary conditions
docs.text: Möbius and \(\pi\)-flux variants test how boundary conditions alter finite graph spectra and gap structure. Observing a gap does not identify a unique mass index or establish a physical mechanism.

docs.title: Evidence vocabulary
docs.text:
The project distinguishes numerical reproduction, preregistered statistical outcomes, fitted relationships, and open conjectures. A fitted relationship \(m=A n\) is not an independently derived prediction; the target set \(\{1,12,17,40\}\) remains unselected by an established invariant.

See Verified Results, Glossary, and Open Problems.

docs.title: Spectral decimation
docs.text: A recursive relation connecting spectral data at successive graph approximations. In this project, the principal scaling factor is approximately five, with corrections for the corner-degree-2 Laplacian.

docs.title: Sierpiński gasket (SG)
docs.text: The self-similar graph used as the main spectral substrate for the documented computations.

docs.title: Spectral dimension
docs.text: The exponent associated with spectral counting. For the Sierpiński gasket, the theoretical value used here is \(d_s/2=\ln 3/\ln 5\approx0.6826\).

docs.title: Fukushima–Shima gaps
docs.text: Forbidden spectral intervals associated with the spectral-decimation structure. The repository reports their finite-level numerical reproduction within the documented setup.

docs.title: Möbius / \(\pi\)-flux boundary condition
docs.text: A boundary twist used to study how flux changes the graph spectrum. The tested full \(\pi\)-flux configuration opens a gap, but this does not establish the target mass-index rule.

docs.title: Target indices
docs.text: The four integers \(\{1,12,17,40\}\) used in the proposed mass relation. Their independent derivation from a spectral invariant has not been established.

docs.title: Look-elsewhere effect
docs.text: The statistical inflation of apparent significance when many configurations, rules, or parameter choices are tested. Phi-Genesis records configuration counts and preregistered decision thresholds to make this risk explicit.

docs.title: Null-only power check
docs.text: A check, designed without looking at target outcomes, that establishes whether a protocol could reach its decision threshold under an idealized target-compatible result.

docs.title: Inertia count
docs.text: The number of eigenvalues below a chosen threshold, computed from the inertia of a shifted matrix. The project's sparse-LU method is numerical and floating-point based, not a machine-checked proof.

docs.title: Evidence labels
docs.text:
• Reproduced numerically: observed again with documented computation and scope.
  • No evidence: the tested protocol did not meet its predeclared threshold.
  • Not reproduced: a prior claim was not obtained in the documented tests.
  • Open: current evidence does not settle the question.
  • Fit, not prediction: parameters or target indices were chosen using the data being matched.

docs.title: Higher moments for the signed Z2-flux Laplacian
docs.text:
Evidence status: exact finite-level integer computations. The observed recurrence is not an all-level theorem and has not been formalized in Lean 4.

This is a separate scalar signed-graph experiment from the noncommutative SU(2) trace-defect results in Evgeny-Theorem.

docs.title: Operator and representative
docs.text:
At level m, let $$ L_m=D_m-A_{s,m}, $$ where D is the ordinary degree matrix and A_s is the signed adjacency matrix. The GF(2) system prescribes one parity equation for each listed hole boundary. The solver sets non-pivot edge variables to zero. Thus every numerical statement below concerns this deterministic representative, not every cocycle satisfying the same hole parities.

For a generation mask t, bit i-1 specifies whether holes of generation i have odd (1) or even (0) boundary parity.

docs.title: Generation-twist recurrence
docs.text:
Let $$ F_m(t_1,\ldots,t_m)=\mathrm{Tr}(L_m(t_1,\ldots,t_m)^{10}). $$

Complete exact sweeps were computed for every mask at levels 4--9 (16, 32, 64, 128, 256, and 512 masks). All 1,008 transitions from level 3 to level 9 satisfy a common correction polynomial: $$ F_{m+1}=3F_m+Q(t_1,t_2,t_3,t_{m+1}). $$ With a=t1, b=t2, c=t3, d=t_(m+1), $$ \begin{aligned} Q(a,b,c,d)={}&127182024+89195520a+73945440b-145153920ab\ &+55360c-150880ac+40320bc-39680abc\ &+d(115347760-110022480a+10024960b\ &\qquad-20854720ab+320c-640ac). \end{aligned} $$ The exceptional 2-to-3 transition has a different correction; see the source module and CSV truth table. At level 10, 156 masks were directly evaluated and all agree with the later recurrence. Other level-10 mask values are predictions, not direct matrix-power calculations. The complete Boolean sweeps are injective: all trace values within each level 4--9 sweep are distinct.

docs.title: Why this is not a hole-flux invariant
docs.text: Hole-boundary parities do not uniquely determine all elementary-triangle holonomies. At level 5 the graph cycle-space rank is 364, while the 121 hole-boundary constraints have rank 121. The audited elementary-triangle patterns retain 243 degrees of freedom. Moving the negative local triangle within one of the four-triangle groups preserves all prescribed hole parities but changes the tenth trace. Therefore the H10 value belongs to the chosen cocycle representative, not to hole flux alone.

docs.title: Exact arithmetic and validation
docs.text: For symmetric real L, $$ \mathrm{Tr}(L^{10})=|L^5|_F^2. $$ The implementation uses integer sparse arithmetic and checks a conservative int64 bound. The optimized boundary walk and packed GF(2) solver are compared with the original geometric boundary scan and dense RREF solver through level 5, including all generation masks at those levels. The regression tests also compare Frobenius and sequential sparse-power traces.

docs.title: Follow-up structural audit — 3 November 2026
docs.text:
The follow-up extended direct generation-mask calculations to every mask at levels 3–9: 1,016 exact traces and 1,008 transition checks. Every checked transition agrees with one correction polynomial \(Q(t_1,t_2,t_3,t_{m+1})\).

A separate three-copy audit checked all 112 masks at parent levels 4–6. It decomposes the correction as \(Q=P+G\): local child-restriction changes give \(P\), while the three pairwise junction-word sums give \(G\). The corner-moment audit contains 336 observations and 48 stable signatures.

At level 5, 243 individual edge flips preserve the prescribed hole parities, yet every one changes H10. Thus 12,387,360 belongs to the chosen deterministic representative family, not to hole flux alone. The exact switching invariant belongs to the full signed-graph switching class.

These remain finite structural checks, not an all-level theorem or a Lean 4 formalization. See the follow-up note, full-flux table, Q truth table, and local perturbation audit.

docs.title: Relation to SU(2) H10
docs.text: The central lift identity $$ \mathrm{Tr}((L\otimes I_2)^{10})=2\mathrm{Tr}(L^{10}) $$ is valid for this scalar L. It does not identify the scalar Z2-flux defect with the SU(2) axis-orientation defect. These are different operators and proof obligations; their coefficients must not be interchanged.

docs.title: Methodology — Testing Spectral Selection Rules
docs.text: This page explains the method used to test whether spectral configurations select the target indices \(T=\{1,12,17,40\}\). The full versioned protocol is maintained in METHODOLOGY.md; the cumulative record is the protocol ledger.

docs.title: The question and the look-elsewhere effect
docs.text:
The mass formula \(m=A n\) fits four selected masses with one scale and four integer indices. The central research question is not whether the fit can be written down, but whether a spectral rule independently selects those indices. Trying many operator configurations makes accidental matches increasingly likely.

The protocol therefore asks whether a configuration scores unusually well relative to null ensembles after taking the maximum over the tested configurations. A striking individual match is not enough.

docs.title: Protocol design
docs.text:
1. Fix the target and rule. Record the target set, index-selection rule, spectral window and tested family before evaluation.
  2. Define null ensembles. Use generic operators of the relevant type to estimate how often each target appears by chance.
  3. Weight by base rate. Common targets should contribute less evidence than rare targets.
  4. Correct for searching many configurations. The test statistic uses the best score across the family, not just a hand-picked configuration.
  5. Check power using null data alone. Confirm that the chosen statistic and threshold can be reached before evaluating the target family.
  6. Use a fixed decision threshold. A candidate must reach \(p\le0.01\) under both specified null ensembles.
  7. Keep a cumulative ledger. Record abandoned, exploratory and related families, and disclose dependence between them.

docs.title: Why the power check matters
docs.text: Protocol v1.0 was unable to reach the decision threshold even if a configuration selected all four targets. Its negative outcome therefore did not meaningfully discriminate the tested family. Later protocols changed \(k\) using null-only design so that the threshold could be reached. Those later tests still did not pass.

docs.title: Interpretation discipline
docs.text: A negative result applies to the tested family, selection rule, parameter range and null model. It does not prove that no mechanism can exist. Conversely, a numerical match after choosing targets and trying many configurations is not a prediction.

docs.title: Open Problems and Research Roadmap
docs.text: The central convergence theorem is established. The items below concern sharper evaluation, asymptotic structure, and extensions of the proved graph-matrix result. Separate physical-application questions are listed at the end and do not affect the principal theorem.

docs.title: 1. Sharper evaluation and analytic characterization of the limit
docs.text:
Question. Can the exact rational enclosure of \(\lambda_\infty\) be sharpened to provide a certified decimal expansion at substantially higher precision, an effective error estimate for finite levels, or an analytic/algebraic characterization?

Established starting point. Lean proves that the least-eigenvalue sequence converges and that

\[ \lambda_\infty\in[L,U],\qquad U-L=2\cdot10^{-36}. \]

This is already an exact existence-and-enclosure theorem. The approximately 145-digit output at level 9 is numerical and must not be substituted for a certified expansion of the infinite-level limit.

Path forward. Derive a quantitative tail estimate for \(|\lambda_\infty-\lambda_N|\) that can be proved uniformly in \(N\), then use outward-rounded interval arithmetic or exact rational bounds to sharpen the enclosure. Investigate closed-form or algebraic descriptions only as a further mathematical question; a closed form is not required for the limit to be a well-defined constant.

docs.title: 2. Prove the all-level quadratic increment law
docs.text:
Question. Do the increments \(\delta_N=\lambda_N-\lambda_{N-1}\) satisfy

\[ \delta_{N+1}\sim c\,\delta_N^2 \]

for a rigorously defined coefficient \(c\)?

Current evidence. High-precision finite-level calculations show ratios approaching approximately \(0.4939504899\) over the reported upper levels. The derivative recursion of the Schur trajectory is formalized, but the uniform derivative bounds and asymptotic argument needed to establish this law have not been proved.

Path forward. Establish uniform control of the differentiated Schur map along the root trajectory, identify the limiting coefficient, and prove a remainder estimate strong enough to justify the asymptotic relation.

docs.title: 3. Unconditional identification with the external \(\theta=2\pi\) operator
docs.text:
Question. Can the recursively defined local-face matrix be identified source-to-source with the external operator denoted by \(\theta=2\pi\)?

The repository proves theorems for its explicitly defined graph matrices and their signed gauge realization. The physical/operator identification requires the external operator's source definition, boundary conventions, vertex/edge ordering, and a proof of exact equivalence. Numerical agreement alone is insufficient.

docs.title: 4. Complete spectral-decimation exceptional set
docs.text:
Question. Can the full recursive exceptional set for the implemented corner-degree-2 graph Laplacian be characterized, including all multiplicities and boundary corrections?

The map \(\phi(\lambda)=\lambda(5-\lambda)\) captures the idealized decimation structure, but the graph's corner convention produces exceptional pairs and residuals that are not yet completely classified. The current diagnostics separate exact matches from near-misses and do not close the full correspondence.

docs.title: 5. Finite-level estimation of the spectral exponent
docs.text:
Question. Can a finite-level estimator recover the asymptotic spectral exponent robustly without depending materially on a chosen log-periodic window?

The theoretical value is \(d_s/2=\ln3/\ln5\approx0.6826\). Ordinary regression fits show finite-level and window bias. The level-9 chord estimator is within 0.1% of its stated comparison expression on the reported \(N\geq1000\) subset, while sliding-window fits still vary with window width and phase. These are complementary results for different estimators; the broader robustness question remains open.

Path forward. Derive an analytical finite-size correction from decimation theory or establish an estimator whose output is stable under reasonable window choices. More levels alone are not expected to remove estimator-window dependence.

See reproducibility instructions and the source scripts in protocol_data.

docs.title: 6. Signed-\(Z_2\) H10: prove the observed generation recurrence
docs.text:
Question. Can the finite-data relation

\[ F_{m+1}(t_1,\ldots,t_{m+1}) =3F_m(t_1,\ldots,t_m)+Q(t_1,t_2,t_3,t_{m+1}) \]

be derived for every level from copy restrictions, corner-moment identities, and the three-copy word expansion?

Exact generation-mask sweeps at levels 4–9 and 1,008 transition checks support one Boolean correction polynomial. At level 10, 156 directly computed masks agree with the recurrence. These checks do not prove the recurrence at arbitrary levels or constitute a Lean 4 formalization. Hole-boundary parities do not determine the complete signed cocycle; local representative choices affect H10.

Path forward. Prove the local restriction identities uniformly in the level, derive the correction polynomial from the word expansion, and formalize the resulting induction. Keep the representative convention explicit.

See the finite H10 research note.

docs.title: Separate historical application: spectral selection for a mass-fit model
docs.text:
An earlier research branch explored whether independently motivated spectral constructions could select the integer labels used in a mass-fit study. The tested protocols, null ensembles, exploratory diagnostics, and their limitations are preserved in the selection-protocol archive, D₃ audit, methodology, and protocol ledger.

This application is logically separate from the Schur recursion and the proof of \(\lambda_\infty\). Its hypotheses and statistical tests are not premises or dependencies of the convergence theorem. The archive remains available for historical completeness and any future independently motivated continuation.

docs.title: Research trail
docs.text:
1. Spectral observations on gasket-like graph families. Initial numerical patterns motivated questions about decimation, gaps, and target indices.
  2. Broader family searches. Additional operator and configuration families were examined; the growing search space made the look-elsewhere effect central to interpretation.
  3. Preregistered tests. The selection hypothesis was tested with declared thresholds and null models. The documented tests did not meet the required threshold.
  4. Methodology correction. Underpowered designs and post-selection risks were explicitly recorded rather than treated as positive evidence.
  5. Current status — v2.2.1. The project reports bounded numerical observations, a still-open finite-window exponent question, and no independently established target-index rule.

docs.title: Reproducibility and Computational Workflow
docs.text: The repository's source code, tests, fixed-seed protocol data and versioned records are the primary reproducibility artifacts. This guide summarizes the commands in the project README; use a clean local clone and follow the cautions below.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
The project uses Python with NumPy and SciPy for numerical work.

pip install numpy scipy
python -c "import phi_genesis; print('OK')"

For editable installation and tests:

pip install -e . pytest
pytest -q -m "not nightly"

The README reports that the fast suite can take roughly 2–3 minutes on one CPU core, with the level-8 test dominating. Nightly tests are excluded by this command.

docs.title: Reproduce signed-Z2 H10 finite calculations
docs.text:
python -m phi_genesis.higher_moments_z2 --validate-reference --max-level 10 --output /tmp/full_flux_h10.csv
pytest -q test_higher_moments_z2.py

The module computes exact integer traces for the deterministic GF(2) representative. The reference boundary scan and dense solver are checked through level 5; see the H10 research note for the finite-data scope and caveats.

docs.title: Reproduce protocol v1.2.1
docs.text:
python -m phi_genesis.selection_protocol_v121 stepA
python -m phi_genesis.selection_protocol_v121 stepB
  • stepA regenerates the null pools using seeds fixed in the code; the README estimates about 15 minutes.
  • stepB runs the evaluation and should be compared with protocol_data/results_v1_2_1.json.
  • Caution: stepA rewrites protocol_data/null_pools_v1_2_1.json. If you want to preserve the committed file exactly, perform the reproduction on a separate working copy.

docs.title: Reproduce Open Problem #2 estimator studies
docs.text:
python protocol_data/op2_window_bias.py table
python protocol_data/op2_window_bias.py sliding
python protocol_data/op2_chord_estimator.py 8 9

The window-bias script uses the cached numerical inertia counts documented by the project. The chord-estimator command compares levels 8 and 9 for the documented estimator.

docs.title: What to record
docs.text:
For a reproducible report, include:

  • Git commit SHA and Python / NumPy / SciPy versions;
  • exact command and test selection;
  • graph level, operator convention, boundary condition and numerical tolerance;
  • protocol version, random seeds and null ensemble;
  • whether an output was regenerated or read from committed data;
  • any deviation from preregistered settings.

A passing test suite validates the tested code paths, not every scientific interpretation in the repository. Numerical results should always be reported with their level, estimator, parameter range and known limitations.

docs.title: Phi-Genesis — Spectral Research Home
docs.text:
The central result of Phi-Genesis is a formally verified convergence theorem for the least eigenvalues of recursively refined Sierpiński-gasket graph operators.

FEATURED MATHEMATICAL RESULT

An exact three-corner Schur boundary recursion is connected to the graph matrices in Lean 4. For every level \(N\geq6\), its selected \(A_1\) root is the unique least eigenvalue in an exact rational interval. The least-eigenvalue sequence converges to \(\lambda_\infty\) in that interval, whose width is \(2\cdot10^{-36}\).

Read the Schur recursion and limiting spectral constant and the Lean proof map.

Phi-Genesis combines formal proof, exact finite-level algebra, and high-precision numerical investigation. The repository keeps these evidence types distinct: the Lean theorem proves existence and enclosure of the limit; the 145-digit level-9 value is a finite-level computation; the observed quadratic correction remains a conjectural asymptotic pattern.

docs.title: Principal mathematical result
docs.text:
\[ \lambda_N=\lambda_{\min}(Q_N),\qquad \lambda_N\longrightarrow\lambda_\infty\in[L,U], \qquad U-L=2\cdot10^{-36}. \]

Here \(Q_N=D_N+A_N\) is the signless graph Laplacian. The specified signed local-face matrix is gauge-conjugate to \(Q_N\) and has the same spectrum.

The exact rational endpoints, theorem names, and proof dependencies are given in the spectral-limit dossier. The separate all-level lower-bound theorem proves that every real eigenvalue of the signed matrix is at least \(1\).

docs.title: Research question
docs.text:
Does any tested operator family on Sierpiński-gasket graph approximations select the target indices \(T=\{1,12,17,40\}\) more often than expected by chance, after accounting for the number of configurations tried?

The target indices were identified from a mass fit; therefore a match is not independent evidence by itself. The selection search uses a look-elsewhere correction over the configurations within each family, null ensembles, target weights based on null base rates, and a predeclared decision threshold of \(p\le0.01\) in both null ensembles.

docs.title: Preregistered results
docs.text:
Protocol Family / rule Configurations Result Power status v1.0 F1 + F2 + F3; \(k=12\), window 60 75 No evidence; p = 0.922 / 0.968 Threshold unreachable; negative is uninformative about whether the family contains a rule. v1.1 Same family; \(k=6\), window 60 75 No evidence; p = 0.966 / 0.997 Threshold reachable; informative negative for these configurations. v1.2.1 SG × S¹ continuum circle, two spin structures; \(k=8\), window 60 10 No evidence; p = 0.953 / 0.926 Threshold reachable; informative negative for these configurations.

The p-value pairs are ordered as documented in the source records (N-pot / N-edge for v1.0 and v1.1; N-circ / N-circpot for v1.2.1). Each pair fails the requirement that both nulls meet the threshold.

The cumulative ledger records 193 configuration evaluations from the documented main families, plus an earlier Sierpiński-carpet search of about 128 level-3 configurations and an unrecorded level-4 sweep. The honest cumulative statement is therefore at least about 321, not an exact exhaustive count.

docs.title: Other relevant checks
docs.text:
• Generation twists: all 32 \(2^5\) configurations at level 5 were tested; maximum target overlap was 1 of 4, and index 40 was never selected.
  • Base-rate audit: under random on-site potentials, the ratio-based rule selected index 1 about 95% of the time, while index 40 appeared about 3.4% of the time. Hits on the four indices are therefore not equally informative.
  • Carpet branch: the early 4/4 match was reassessed against a null model; the record attributes it to a look-elsewhere effect and marks that branch abandoned.
  • v1.0 power correction: even a configuration selecting all four targets would not have reached the required p-value. This was documented as a limitation of that protocol rather than treated as evidence against all possible mechanisms.

docs.title: Exploratory D₃ representation audit (not preregistered)
docs.text: The six barycentric-coordinate permutations were verified as graph automorphisms at levels 5–7. The first 60 positive-spectrum cluster signatures agree numerically across those levels. Corrected target clusters: 1–2 (E), 12–14 (A1 + E), 16–17 (E), 30–41 (3A1 + A2 + 4E). The “contains A1” criterion hits 12 and 40 only; the simple-A1 criterion hits none. This corrects an earlier off-by-one report that included the zero mode. The calculation is numerical, not a Lean proof or exact-arithmetic certificate. See full D₃ audit.

docs.title: v1.3 ancestry/decimation archive: pending verification
docs.text: A prior-session summary reports a probe based on phi(lambda)=lambda(5-lambda), but the archive, runnable source, frozen inputs, and expected outputs were not present in the inspected repository snapshot. Its results are not independently verified here and are excluded from the verified result table and configuration count. Add the complete archive and reproduce it using the preregistered positive-spectrum indexing before promoting it to verified status.

docs.title: What the result means
docs.text:
The tested families did not satisfy the preregistered selection criterion. This is a bounded negative result: it does not prove that no operator family could select the indices. It does mean the current mass formula cannot be described as a spectral prediction.

Any new family must have an a-priori rationale and a new preregistration, with null-only power design completed before target evaluation. Re-running the same search on the same four targets would increase the look-elsewhere burden rather than resolve it.

docs.title: Schur Recursion and the Limiting Spectral Constant
docs.text: Principal result. The least eigenvalues of the recursively defined Sierpiński-gasket graph Laplacians form a convergent sequence. The convergence theorem, the least-eigenvalue identification, and the exact rational enclosure are formalized in Lean 4.

docs.title: 1. Operator and graph sequence
docs.text:
Let \(Q_N=D_N+A_N\) be the signless graph Laplacian of the level-\(N\) Sierpiński-gasket graph. The signed local-face matrix is

\[ H_N=D_N+A_{s,N}. \]

The Lean development proves that the signed matrix is diagonally gauge-conjugate to the signless matrix:

\[ H_N=G_N Q_N G_N, \]

where \(G_N\) is the diagonal vertex-gauge matrix and \(G_N^2=I\). Hence the two finite matrices have the same spectrum.

Write \(\lambda_N\) for their common least eigenvalue.

docs.title: 2. Exact three-corner Schur recursion
docs.text:
Eliminating the interior vertices leaves a three-corner boundary response. By the \(S_3\) symmetry of the boundary, it is described by a diagonal coefficient \(\alpha_N(\lambda)\) and an off-diagonal coefficient \(\beta_N(\lambda)\). The distinguished scalar characteristic is the constant-boundary channel:

$ F_N(\lambda)=a_N(\lambda)+2b_N(\lambda). $

The exact Schur update is connected to the actual recursively assembled graph matrices. The formal proof covers the midpoint pivots, the boundary-response bridge, and the nonnegativity/inertia argument needed to identify the selected root with the least eigenvalue.

docs.title: 3. The Lean convergence theorem
docs.text:
For every \(N=6+n\), the selected \(A_1\) root is the unique root of \(F_N\) in the exact interval \([L,U]\) and equals the least eigenvalue of \(Q_N\). The least-eigenvalue sequence converges:

\[ \exists\,\lambda_\infty\in[L,U],\qquad \lambda_N\longrightarrow\lambda_\infty \quad(N\to\infty). \]

The interval endpoints are exact rationals:

\[ L=\frac{1309128920280813421888623088170810187}{10^{36}}, \qquad U=\frac{1309128920280813421888623088170810189}{10^{36}}. \] \[ U-L=2\cdot10^{-36}, \qquad \lambda_\infty\in[L,U]. \]

This is an exact existence-and-enclosure theorem, not a floating-point estimate. The limiting value is also proved to be a zero of the uniformly limiting \(A_1\) characteristic.

The formal proof chain includes:

Mathematical step Lean theorem Source Signed/signless gauge equivalence sgSignedLaplacianMatrix_eq_gauge_conj SchurBridge.lean Graph-matrix boundary response follows the Schur recursion sgCornerResponse_trajectory_bootstrap SchurCornerTrajectory.lean Root uniqueness in \([L,U]\) schurBootstrapA1Root_unique SchurLambdaMin.lean Selected root is the least eigenvalue sgChosenRoot_isLeast SchurEigenvalue.lean Least-eigenvalue convergence sgLeastEigenvalue_converges SchurEigenvalue.lean Limit is a zero of the limiting characteristic schurBootstrapA1AtLevel_rootLimit_is_root SchurBoundary.lean Transfer to the signed matrix sgSignedLeastEigenvalue_converges SchurSignedTransfer.lean Uniform lower bound at every level sgSignedLaplacianMatrix_eigenvalue_ge_one SignedLaplacianMatrix.lean

The uniform lower bound \(1\) is a separate all-level theorem. It does not replace the convergence theorem; it provides an independent positive lower bound for every refinement level.

docs.title: 4. Numerical finite-level values
docs.text:
The high-precision Schur calculation reports the following bottom eigenvalues:

Level \(N\) Dimension Finite-level numerical \(\lambda_N\) 4 123 \(1.3091289186270032373372269265507617266049\ldots\) 5 366 \(1.3091289202808134205376249464114593830015\ldots\) 9 29,526 \(1.3091289202808134218886230881708101885523\ldots\)

The level-9 calculation is stable to about 145 displayed decimal places in the high-precision run. Those are digits of a finite-level computation. They are not a 145-digit certified expansion of \(\lambda_\infty\).

The observed ratios

\[ \frac{\lambda_{N+1}-\lambda_N} {(\lambda_N-\lambda_{N-1})^2} \approx0.4939504899 \]

are numerical evidence for a quadratic increment law. The all-level law and its coefficient have not yet been proved.

See the high-precision computation note and the reproducible Schur script.

docs.title: 5. What remains open
docs.text:
1. Sharpen the rigorously certified enclosure of \(\lambda_\infty\) and seek an analytic or algebraic characterization where one exists.
  2. Prove the all-level quadratic increment law and determine its coefficient.
  3. Prove an unconditional source-to-source identification of this local-face matrix model with the external \(\theta=2\pi\) operator.
  4. Complete the characterization of the exceptional set for the graph's spectral-decimation correspondence.

These are refinements and extensions of the established convergence theorem. They do not negate the theorem or its exact rational enclosure.

docs.title: 6. Reproduction
docs.text:
From the repository root:

lake build PhiGenesis
python -m pip install mpmath
python computational/spectral_gap_theta_2pi/schur_bottom_eigenvalue.py

The Lean build checks the formal theorem. The Python calculation reproduces finite-level numerical values; it is not used as a premise in the Lean proof.

Primary sources: the Lean proof map, Schur boundary recursion, least-eigenvalue theorem, and signed transfer.

docs.title: Verified Results and Evidence Boundaries
docs.text: This page puts the principal mathematical result first and distinguishes formal theorems from finite-level numerical and computational records.

docs.title: 1. Schur recursion and convergence of the least eigenvalue
docs.text:
For the signless graph Laplacian \(Q_N=D_N+A_N\), the exact three-corner Schur recursion selects a unique \(A_1\) root in an exact rational interval for each \(N\geq6\). Lean 4 proves that this root is the least eigenvalue and that the least-eigenvalue sequence converges to \(\lambda_\infty\) in that interval.

The endpoints are exact rationals:

\[ L=\frac{1309128920280813421888623088170810187}{10^{36}}, \qquad U=\frac{1309128920280813421888623088170810189}{10^{36}}. \] \[ \lambda_\infty\in[L,U], \qquad U-L=2\cdot10^{-36}. \]

The signed local-face matrix is gauge-conjugate to \(Q_N\), so it has the same spectrum. The limiting value is also a zero of the limiting \(A_1\) characteristic.

Lean theorems: schurBootstrapA1Root_unique, sgChosenRoot_isLeast, sgLeastEigenvalue_converges, sgSignedLeastEigenvalue_converges, and schurBootstrapA1AtLevel_rootLimit_is_root.

See the spectral-limit dossier, proof map, and source files SchurLambdaMin.lean and SchurEigenvalue.lean.

docs.title: 2. Uniform lower bound for the signed graph Laplacian
docs.text:
Every real eigenvalue of the explicitly defined signed graph Laplacian, represented by a nonzero real eigenvector, is at least \(1\) at every refinement level. The matrix is expressed as a sum of rank-one edge contributions, and its quadratic form is identified with the signed graph energy.

Lean theorem: sgSignedLaplacianMatrix_eigenvalue_ge_one in SignedLaplacianMatrix.lean.

docs.title: 3. Sierpiński-gasket spectral structure
docs.text:
• Spectral decimation: the characteristic eigenvalue scale factor is 5 between consecutive levels, with corner-defect corrections for the corner-degree-2 Laplacian used in this repository.
  • Fukushima–Shima gaps: computations recover forbidden zones associated with fixed points near \(\lambda\approx2.5\) and \(\lambda\approx3\).
  • Log-periodic structure: counting data exhibit the expected periodic signature associated with the factor-five scaling.

These statements concern the graph family, operator convention, and finite-level checks documented in the source. They are numerical/computational observations, not substitutes for the Lean convergence theorem.

docs.title: 4. Spectral dimension and finite-level estimates
docs.text:
For the Sierpiński gasket, the theoretical exponent is

\[ \frac{d_s}{2}=\frac{\ln3}{\ln5}\approx0.6826. \]

The repository reports that a window-free chord estimator is within 0.1% of its stated comparison expression at level 9 for the documented \(N\geq1000\) subset. This is a result for that estimator and range, not proof that every finite-level estimator converges uniformly. The inertia-based count path uses Sylvester's law of inertia with sparse LU; the documented level-10 graph has 88,575 vertices.

See Open Problem 5 and the reproduction guide.

docs.title: 5. Möbius and \(\pi\)-flux boundary conditions
docs.text:
For the tested level-5 graph, the documented full-\(\pi\)-flux configuration raises the first eigenvalue from approximately 0.006 to approximately 0.46, opening a spectral gap in that instance. Partial twists also produce gaps in the tested cases.

These are finite-level boundary-condition results for the stated graph and operator convention. They form a separate computational strand and are not used as premises in the Schur-limit proof.

docs.title: 6. Signed-\(Z_2\) H10 finite computation
docs.text:
For the deterministic GF(2) representative used by the hole-boundary solver, exact sparse-integer calculations give

\[ D_m^{(10)}= \operatorname{Tr}(L_{\pi,m}^{10})- \operatorname{Tr}(L_{0,m}^{10}). \]

The traces are computed through level 10. The residual \(D_m^{(10)}-3D_{m-1}^{(10)}\) equals 12,387,360 on transitions 3→4 through 9→10. Complete generation-twist sweeps were computed at levels 4–9, with 1,008 transition checks; 156 level-10 samples agree with the recurrence. The recurrence is not yet an all-level theorem.

Hole-boundary parities do not determine a unique cocycle. At level 5, 243 elementary-triangle holonomy degrees of freedom remain, and changing the local representative while preserving hole parities changes H10. This is not a topological invariant of hole flux alone. The scalar signed operator is distinct from the SU(2) operator in Evgeny-Theorem.

See the full finite H10 note, implementation, and reproduction instructions.

docs.title: 7. Separate historical physical applications
docs.text:
The repository retains an exploratory integer-index mass-fit study and its associated spectral-selection protocols as a distinct research archive. Those records document their own assumptions, numerical calculations, statistical design, and limitations. They are not part of the definition or proof dependency graph of the limiting spectral constant.

For those records, see Selection Protocol, D₃ Representation Audit, Methodology, and Protocol Ledger.

docs.title: 8. η-invariant claim — not reproduced
docs.text: The RFT-String v8.7 claim \(\bar\eta(0)=-4\) for the stated boundary potential was not reproduced. The documented test reports asymmetry +1 for the claimed potential, −1 for a random potential, and −2 for zero potential; −4 was not observed in the tested cases. The repository interprets the observed asymmetry as a finite-size effect, not as a demonstrated topological invariant.

docs.title: 9. How to read the evidence
docs.text:
Label Interpretation Theoretical identity Follows from specified mathematical definitions and assumptions. Lean 4 formal theorem A proposition accepted by the Lean kernel for the stated definitions and assumptions. Reproducible numerical result A computation can be rerun for the documented finite instance and implementation. Fit / estimator output Depends on model choice, parameter range, and estimator design. Open problem Current evidence is incomplete or a proof obligation remains.

The finite-level numerical results are not automatically formal proofs. The Lean-verified status of Evgeny's Theorem does not transfer to this repository: the operator families, observables, and verification methods differ.
